verdict.rationale: Phaser itself is an open-source (MIT) code library where games are just plain JS/TS and standard web assets (JSON, images, audio), so there's no proprietary data format to be locked into by design. The only direct evidence on 'leaving' comes from the paid Phaser Editor: games created aren't tied to the licence and project files can be transferred to VS Code (phaser-docs-41), suggesting no lock-in, but there is no explicit 'export all your data' feature, data-export tooling, or documentation framed around portability/openness for AI-native users. Missing for 10: an explicit data/project export feature or open-format export documentation, and independent confirmation that Editor projects are fully portable outside the paid tool.
